newsitem.title: UK: China zinc mine imports, metal exports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: China zinc mine imports, metal exports seen rising.

text.p: China's imports of zinc concentrates and exports of refined zinc metal are likely to rise over the next few years, according to the latest weekly report from Billiton Metals.
"Rising Western mine production should see higher Chinese imports of concentrates...leading to higher exports of metal to the West in 1997 and 1998," Billiton said in the report.
The expected rise in zinc prices over the period would encourage the trend, the report added.

Billiton forecast zinc smelting capacity to rise to 1.455 million tonnes in 1997 from 1.405 million this year and 1.23 million in 1995. The total is expected to rise to 1.580 million by the year 2000.
However, the actual increase could fall short of estimates, given the limited amount of zinc concentrates produced in China.
The country's reliance on zinc concentrate imports is expected to rise.

"Given that domestic mine supplies are expected to continue to fall short of the country's rising smelting capacity, Chinese imports of zinc concentrates are likely to increase at a pretty steady pace," the report said.
Billiton quoted a Chinese metals official as saying recently that China's consumption of zinc metal would increase 6.6 percent annually, reaching 900,000 tonnes by 2000.
Growth would slow to around 2.9 percent annually during the following ten years, he is quoted as saying.
